artifact: Repaired tracked artifact Owner-path safety contract

overall.one_line_summary: Personal absolute paths were removed from tracked artifacts, the legacy launcher now fails closed without an explicit Owner-local root, and a deterministic tracked-artifact regression prevents recurrence.
strengths: The MLflow design uses a portable environment-variable example instead of a personal path.
The legacy P1 launcher no longer infers a protected data location and exits before execution when MYIS_LEGACY_DAPFAM_ROOT is absent.
The regression scans canonical and generated tracked artifact roots while excluding Owner-authored notes and local Obsidian state.
Focused P2 preflight tests passed 39 and the launcher fail-closed probe returned exit code 2 without protected access.
The full suite passed 294 tests; Dashboard/API passed 21 tests; two full report checks returned no drift.
Session, assets, advisor, layout, P2 closure, archive-runtime, MLflow doctor, Brain literature, Ruff, and whitespace validations passed.
weaknesses: Source and test fixtures remain outside the artifact scan because they may intentionally contain unsafe-path examples used for negative testing.

strengths: The regression covers the tracked artifact roots named by the repository reporting and evidence contract.
Adding a Windows drive path or macOS/Linux home path to the scanned tracked artifacts now fails the deterministic suite with an exact file and line locator.
weaknesses: Non-home POSIX absolute paths are not rejected by this specific Owner-path regression.
suggestions: Continue relying on schema-specific repository-relative path validators for general absolute-path rejection.

strengths: The repair changes repository path safety only and preserves proposal, campaign, budget, gate, and counter state.
The no-Owner-path closeout claim is now supported by both direct repair and a repository-level regression.
The original contradiction remains preserved in a separate Weak Reject audit and is linked to this recovery.
The repair combines explicit configuration, fail-closed execution behavior, tracked-file enumeration, focused tests, and a no-protected-access probe.
weaknesses: Remote CI is recorded separately as Draft PR evidence and is not claimed by this local repair audit.
suggestions: Retain the full validation sequence before requesting Owner review.

findings.observation: The regression intentionally excludes source code, test fixtures, Owner Notes, Obsidian local state, and canvas files.
findings.reasoning: Those surfaces either contain negative-test examples or are explicitly Owner-authored/local and should not be interpreted as generated repository artifacts.
findings.suggestion: Keep the exclusions explicit and review any future expansion of generated artifact roots.
